acceptance.given: A pinned semantic result has bound diagnostic categories and a fresh checkout has the pinned replay inputs available.

oracle.expected: Fresh replay evidence contains diagnostic categories equal to the pinned semantic result categories.
forbidden: A semantic reproduction claim with different diagnostic categories.
Diagnostic categories inferred from labels or prose.
Replay evidence produced before reconstruction of the pinned inputs.
oracle.observable: Machine-verifiable pinned and fresh replay diagnostic-category fields and their equality comparison.

acceptance.then: The fresh replay establishes equality of the pinned and replayed diagnostic categories.
acceptance.when: The toolchain reconstructs pinned inputs and produces fresh replay diagnostic output.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Replay a pinned semantic result with a diagnostic-category mismatch and require semantic reproduction to fail.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Rebuild the pinned input identities before fresh replay and compare machine-verifiable fresh diagnostic categories with the pinned semantic result.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Replay evidence remains non-authorizing and preserves existing terminal-category compatibility while adding no inferred diagnostic equivalence.

slice_hint.state_transition: pinned diagnostic categories without fresh equality proof -> reconstructed pinned identities -> fresh replay -> machine-verified diagnostic-category equality or failed reproduction
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: A fresh replay, after reconstructing the pinned identities, has machine-verifiable diagnostic categories exactly equal to the pinned semantic result.

acceptance.given: Declared repair and runtime evidence boundaries exist and historical evidence content is retained as an immutable baseline.

oracle.expected: The boundary check shows new evidence only as appended content within declared boundaries while prior evidence bytes remain retained.
oracle.observable: Pre-write and post-write evidence-boundary comparison performed by the toolchain evidence handler.

acceptance.then: Repair and runtime evidence is append-only within declared boundaries and historical evidence remains unchanged.
acceptance.when: The toolchain records repair or runtime evidence and evaluates the write boundary.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Attempt an evidence write that overwrites, deletes, or escapes its declared append-only boundary.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Enforce append-only evidence recording within declared boundaries and reject overwrite, deletion, or out-of-bound evidence writes.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Existing historical evidence remains immutable; evidence-record representation changes must remain append-only and non-authorizing.

slice_hint.state_transition: retained historical evidence and declared boundary -> attempted repair/runtime evidence recording -> appended in-bound evidence or rejected integrity violation
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The boundary comparison proves retained prior evidence and permits only appended repair/runtime evidence within the declared boundary.

acceptance.given: A Consumer Manifest transition omission or applicability exception is presented for evaluation.

oracle.expected: The Toolchain validation records an explicit pre-execution exception binding that identifies an existing authorized repository or ADR owner and binds that approval to the omitted Consumer transition; otherwise it rejects the omission.
forbidden: A Consumer transition is omitted without approval from an existing authorized repository or ADR owner.
An unbound, post-execution, or merely asserted exception is treated as valid.
The default transition requirement is treated as exempt before confirmation and binding.
oracle.observable: The Consumer-transition validation result identifies the omitted transition, its pre-bound authorized owner reference, and its acceptance or rejection decision.

acceptance.then: The omission is accepted only when the required authorized exception is already bound; otherwise the transition remains required and the evaluation rejects the omission.
acceptance.when: The Consumer Manifest is frozen or a Consumer transition omission or applicability exception is evaluated.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Evaluate an omitted Consumer transition with no pre-bound approval from an existing authorized repository or ADR owner; require the Consumer-transition validation to reject the omission rather than treating it as an exemption.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Make the Toolchain Consumer-transition validator fail closed: an omission is legal only when a pre-execution, explicit exception binding names an existing authorized repository or ADR owner and binds that authority to the precise omitted Consumer transition. No default exemption, role-name assertion, or unbound exception is accepted.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Validation-only Consumer-exception enforcement: retain existing Consumer route and receipt compatibility while removing only acceptance of an omission lacking a pre-bound authorized-owner exception.

slice_hint.state_transition: Consumer transition omission proposed -> authorized and transition-bound exception verified before execution, or omission rejected and transition remains applicable.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: For every evaluated Consumer-transition omission, the validation result accepts it only when its pre-execution binding identifies an existing authorized repository or ADR owner and the exact omitted transition; all absent, asserted-only, post-execution, or unbound exceptions produce rejection.

acceptance.given: A retained evaluation-seed record is submitted through the Toolchain replay seed-manifest validation path with all non-classification fields otherwise valid.

oracle.expected: The validator accepts the record only when its classification is exactly one of anchor_candidate, challenge_candidate, or non_baseline_exploratory_candidate; every other value, including a baseline or promotion classification, is rejected before a replay result can be accepted.
forbidden: Acceptance based only on a schema field being present without closed-set membership validation.
oracle.observable: The validation result identifies the submitted seed classification and reports rejection for a value outside the three permitted non-baseline classifications.

acceptance.then: The retained seed is classified only within the closed permitted set, preserving its non-baseline status.
acceptance.when: The replay path validates retained evaluation-seed manifest records.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Submit an otherwise-valid retained seed record whose classification is baseline, accepted_baseline, or another value outside the three-value closed set and require the validation invocation to reject it.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Enforce the evaluation-seed classification as a closed non-baseline set at replay seed-manifest validation: only anchor_candidate, challenge_candidate, and non_baseline_exploratory_candidate are valid retained-seed classifications.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No retained seed may remain valid through an unapproved, baseline, or promotion classification; existing records using one of the three permitted values remain compatible.

slice_hint.state_transition: An otherwise retained seed record moves from unvalidated classification input to accepted only after exact membership in the three permitted non-baseline classifications is established.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Validation deterministically rejects every retained seed classification outside anchor_candidate, challenge_candidate, and non_baseline_exploratory_candidate, while accepting each permitted value when the record is otherwise valid.
